inside: /* ---------- 30. PAYING FOR HEAT PROTECTION ---------- */
// How protection is paid for, delivered and kept going. Shown in Act on it, and in steps 3 and 4 of Plan a response.
// Draws on two Global Asia Insurance Partnership reports (2026), checked page by page. The parametric report did not evaluate
// consumer outcomes, contracts, pricing or trigger performance: use it for design questions, not as proof that a heat product works.
// cases: say who paid, who received, what it made possible, what it left out and whether it continued. Where sources disagree, say so.

name: FINANCE
inside: // fields saved with the plan, in step 3
// When heat reaches lenders: insights from a 2026 commentary, summarised in our words and attributed. Opinion, not a study.
// An exercise for funders, officials and NGOs: follow one worker’s money through a heatwave week, build protection, then test it.
// The people are composites, not real individuals. Numbers are illustrative Indian rupees a day, and every one can be changed.
// The tool only adds up cash. It never predicts illness, productivity or payouts, and never gives a score.
// effect: hours = working hours recovered on hot days (an assumption, shown on the card); water = no need to buy water at work;
// rentfree = no work cost on hot days; keepbonus = illness does not cost the attendance bonus;
// people: protect = share of daily pay that heat cannot cut (a monthly wage); bonus = lost if ill; amounts = local payment sizes;
// defaults = measures already in place by law; mtext = local names, descriptions and conditions for a measure.
// rest = paid hours protected; freecare = no doctor fee; money = a payment (amount, arrival day); hospital = pays only if admitted.
// conds: what has to be true for the person to actually use it. A measure counts only when every condition holds,
// except a soft condition, which changes the cost but not whether it can be used. start: false means it starts unmet; auto: met by another measure.

name: HEAT_WEEK
inside: // countries: currency (sym, loc, dp = decimals), the hot week's temperatures, and real context, each with a source
/* ---------- 33. MAKE IT WORK TOGETHER: PROTECTION IN A PLACE ---------- */
// A coordinator's simulation, on its own page (/together/, together.js). Three hypothetical places, each with
// composite workers, the bodies whose agreement protection depends on, and measures broken into the requirements
// that must all hold. A requirement counts only at the status it needs, and "agreed" or beyond counts only with
// evidence. Work is measured in hours of dangerous heat and days' pay, never as a score or a prediction of illness.
// expo = hours a hot day keeps someone in dangerous heat; loss = share of a day's pay heat costs them.
// measure.helps: hours and pay a working measure gives back each hot day; once = paid once, on day 1, if it works.
// req.need = the status it must reach; req.from = the day of the hot week from which an unmet requirement breaks it.

name: PLACE_SIM
